title: Nourishing Eggplant and Potato Curry
subtitle: with Quinoa
description: When it comes to veggie curry, eggplant and potato is a classic combo. With the Indian spice level set to mild and served with nutritious quinoa, this wholesome dish certainly hits the spot!

steps.text: Cook quinoa: Rinse the quinoa well in a sieve, then drain. Put the quinoa in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 12-15 mins until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Cut the eggplant into 2cm chunks (see Make it yours). Halve the leek lengthwise and thinly slice the pale stem, discarding any dark green stem. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Peel the potato and cut into 2cm chunks. Put the potato in a medium saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 8 mins or until just tender. Drain.

Soften eggplant: Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the curry leaves for 20-30 secs until bright green. Add the eggplant to the pan and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring, for 4 mins or until browned. Remove the curry leaves and eggplant from the pan.

Simmer curry: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the same pan over medium heat. Cook the leek and garlic, stirring, for 4 mins or until softened. Add 1 tbs curry powder and cook for 30 secs or until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, 1 tsp soy sauce and 250ml (1 cup) water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 10 mins or until the sauce is slightly thickened.

Serve up: Add the eggplant and potato to the curry, then cover and cook for a further 6-8 mins until the veggies are tender. Divide the quinoa and curry among bowls, top with the curry leaves and enjoy!

Make it yours: For another spin on this recipe, you might like to roast the eggplant instead of pan-frying it. Drizzle the eggplant chunks with olive oil and roast in the oven at 220C for 20 mins or until browned, before adding to the curry in Step 5. You don't have to fry the curry leaves either; simply add to the curry along with the tomatoes and water.
